metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Household Finance Brokerage Platform domain: the mortgage journeys from online simulation and feasibility certificate through appointment, 25-bank comparison, credit file, bank approval, notary deed and loan-linked insurance, plus refinancing and renovation cases; the comparison-and-switch journeys for insurance across 11 insurers, energy (meter type, digital meter, solar panels) and telecom under BIPT Easy Switch, with contract monitoring and customer care in Hasselt and Oujda; and the network, partner and compliance journeys (about 70 franchised offices, the academy training about 30 advisors a year, more than 50 partners' tariffs and commissions, FSMA and GDPR) that keep a commission-funded, free-for-the-household brokerage running.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (bank mortgage systems of the 25 compared lenders, insurer quote-and-bind systems, energy suppliers and the VREG V-test, telecom operators and BIPT Easy Switch, notaries and e-signature, telephony and chat, the FSMA registers, the Central Individual Credit Register, examination providers and finance systems) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Mortgage Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a first online simulation to the notary deed: feasibility certificates, appointments in about 70 offices or by video call, the same-screen comparison of 25 banks, the bank-ready credit file, approval, insurance and closing, and the refinancing, renovation, second-home and new-build cases of existing owners. These journeys are the core of hypotheek.winkel and the way one mortgage starts a household relationship.

streams.name: Simulate and Check Mortgage Feasibility
streams.description: Take a buyer from a first online question to a document a seller trusts: the hypotheek.winkel and peasy.be simulators (how much can I borrow, monthly repayment, interest rate, financial plan, notary costs, repayment table) turn salary, savings and the intended purchase into a borrowing capacity, the feasibility check compares that situation against the daily conditions of 25 banks and accounts for the renovation obligation of low-EPC homes, and the resulting feasibility certificate (haalbaarheidscertificaat) is what the buyer shows a seller to prove the bid is financeable. Every simulation is also the start of a lead that can become an appointment in one of the ~70 offices.
outcomes: Buyers get a borrowing capacity, monthly repayment and notary-cost estimate within minutes of opening a simulator, so simulation completion rate stays high
Feasibility certificate issuance rate rises and certified buyers lose fewer bids to financing uncertainty
Simulation-to-appointment conversion rises because every saved simulation is a routed lead for the nearest office rather than an anonymous page view

flows.title: From Online Simulation to Feasibility Certificate
flows.description: A first-time buyer runs the borrowing-capacity and monthly-repayment simulators, adds notary costs and a financial plan, requests a feasibility check on a home found on a property portal and receives a certificate to show the seller.
flows.trigger: A buyer has found a home or wants to know their budget before visiting homes and opens a simulator on peasy.be or hypotheekwinkel.be.
flows.successSignal: The buyer holds a feasibility certificate for a concrete purchase price, the seller accepts the bid subject to financing and an appointment with an expert is booked.

steps.title: Run the borrowing-capacity and monthly-repayment simulators
keyFacts: The simulators (hoeveel kan ik lenen, maandlast, rentevoet, aflossingstabel) take net income, existing loans, savings and the desired term and return a borrowing capacity and a monthly repayment for the buyer's situation.
Results are shown in Dutch or French on the brand the buyer entered through, and the buyer can save the result by leaving an e-mail address, which creates a lead.
painPoints: Buyers enter gross instead of net income or forget a car loan, so the simulated capacity is higher than what any of the 25 banks will approve.
A buyer who does not leave contact details disappears after the simulation and never reaches an office.

dependencies.name: Borrowing Capacity and Monthly Repayment Simulator
dependencies.how: Computes borrowing capacity, monthly repayment and repayment table from income, loans, savings and term.

dependencies.name: Multi-brand Site Shell and Language Routing
dependencies.how: Serves the simulator under the right brand and language and keeps the buyer inside one front door.

dependencies.name: Lead Routing and Distribution
dependencies.how: Turns a saved simulation with contact details into a lead for the nearest office.

steps.title: Calculate notary costs and the financial plan
keyFacts: The notary-cost calculator adds registration duties, notary fees and mortgage registration costs to the purchase price so the buyer sees the total amount to finance and the own contribution needed.
The financial plan combines purchase price, renovation budget, own savings and the simulated loan into one overview the buyer can bring to the office.
painPoints: Buyers underestimate the costs on top of the purchase price and discover at the office that their savings do not cover them.
Regional differences in registration duties confuse buyers looking in both Flanders and Brussels.

dependencies.name: Notary Costs and Financial Plan Calculator
dependencies.how: Computes notary and registration costs and assembles the financial plan for the intended purchase.

dependencies.name: Content, Blog and FAQ Pages
dependencies.how: Links the calculator to FAQ and blog articles that explain each cost line.

steps.title: Request a feasibility check for a specific home
keyFacts: The feasibility check compares salary and savings with the conditions of 25 banks for a concrete purchase price and takes into account the Flemish renovation obligation for homes with a low EPC label.
The buyer enters the address or EPC label of the home, the intended bid and any renovation budget; the check returns whether at least one bank would finance the project.
painPoints: Buyers do not know the EPC label of the home they want to bid on, so the renovation obligation is missed until the file stage.
A check run on outdated income data produces a certificate the expert later has to withdraw.

dependencies.name: Feasibility Check and Certificate
dependencies.how: Runs the multi-bank feasibility check for the purchase price, EPC label and renovation budget.

dependencies.name: Borrowing Capacity and Monthly Repayment Simulator
dependencies.how: Reuses the saved simulation inputs so the buyer does not retype income and savings.

steps.title: Issue the feasibility certificate
keyFacts: An expert validates the check, corrects assumptions if needed and issues the haalbaarheidscertificaat as a PDF that states the maximum financeable amount for the project without naming a bank.
The certificate is free, carries the office and expert details and is what the buyer shows the seller or estate agent to strengthen a bid.
painPoints: When several buyers bid on the same home in a hot market, a certificate that arrives a day late costs the buyer the home.
Sellers unfamiliar with the certificate ask for a bank pre-approval instead and the expert has to explain the difference.

dependencies.name: Feasibility Check and Certificate
dependencies.how: Generates and stores the certificate PDF with expert validation and validity period.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator
dependencies.how: Links the certificate to the office and expert that will handle the appointment.

steps.title: Show the certificate to the seller and book the appointment
keyFacts: The buyer sends the certificate to the seller or agent with the bid; hypotheek.winkel positions it as the way to buy with certainty in a market where bids are made subject to financing.
The certificate page invites the buyer to book an office or video appointment so the expert can turn the check into a real comparison once the bid is accepted.
painPoints: The bid is accepted with a short suspensive-condition deadline, leaving the buyer and expert little time to get a real approval.
The buyer books the appointment in a distant office because the locator did not recognise the postcode.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator
dependencies.how: Books the follow-up office or video appointment tied to the certificate and lead.

dependencies.name: Analytics and Data Platform
dependencies.how: Tracks simulation-to-certificate-to-appointment conversion per brand and office.

streams.name: Book and Hold an Advisory Appointment
streams.description: Turn a website, callback, chat or upload request into a held appointment with the right expert: the office locator finds the nearest of about 70 hypotheek.winkels across Flanders and Brussels, the buyer chooses an office visit or a video call, the lead engine routes the request to that office, the expert receives the simulation, uploaded documents and questions in advance, reminders reduce no-shows, and the appointment ends with a clear next step. Appointments are the currency of the franchise network: the brand generates them, the offices convert them.
outcomes: Every website, callback or upload request becomes an appointment in the nearest office or by video call within one working day
The share of appointments held with the buyer's simulation, certificate or uploaded proposal attached in advance rises, so the first meeting is a comparison rather than an intake
No-show rate falls and Appointment-to-loan conversion rate rises because confirmations, reminders and rerouting are systematic

flows.title: From Website Request to a Held Appointment
flows.description: A buyer books an appointment online or asks to be called back, the request is routed to the nearest office, confirmed, prepared and held either in the office or by video call.
flows.trigger: A buyer clicks 'maak een afspraak' or 'bel me terug' on peasy.be or hypotheekwinkel.be, or an uploaded proposal needs an expert conversation.
flows.successSignal: The appointment took place with a prepared expert, the buyer knows the next step and the lead status in the office dashboard is updated.

steps.title: Choose the nearest office or a video call
keyFacts: The office locator lists the ~70 hypotheek.winkels with address, opening hours and experts, and the buyer picks a slot in the office or a video call at a time that suits them, including evenings where offices offer them.
The booking captures the project type (first home, next home, second home, new build, refinancing, self-employed, renovation loan) so the right expert is assigned.
painPoints: Buyers in Wallonia or the German-speaking community find no nearby office and abandon the booking before Meilleurtaux offices are integrated.
Slots shown online are not synchronised with the expert's own calendar, so double bookings happen.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator
dependencies.how: Finds the nearest office, shows available slots and books the office or video appointment.

dependencies.name: Office and Franchise Management
dependencies.how: Provides office addresses, opening hours and the roster of experts per office.

steps.title: Capture a callback or chat request instead
keyFacts: Buyers who prefer not to book directly ask for a callback or start a chat; the request is logged as a ticket and answered by phone within the published opening hours.
Callback requests capture phone number, preferred time, language and topic and are the main entry point for mobile visitors.
painPoints: Callbacks requested on Friday afternoon wait until Monday, and the buyer has already talked to their own bank by then.
Chat conversations that end without an appointment are not followed up.

dependencies.name: Callback and Chat Requests
dependencies.how: Captures the callback or chat request with contact details, topic and preferred time.

dependencies.name: Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox
dependencies.how: Creates the ticket that customer care works until the buyer has an appointment or an answer.

steps.title: Route the lead to the office and expert
keyFacts: The lead engine assigns each request to the office covering the buyer's postcode and to an available expert with the right project experience, respecting the franchise territories.
Leads from uploaded proposals and simulations carry their context so the expert sees what the buyer already knows.
painPoints: Territory disputes between neighbouring franchisees when a buyer lives on the border of two office areas.
Leads routed to an office where the only expert is on leave sit unanswered for days.

dependencies.name: Lead Routing and Distribution
dependencies.how: Applies territory, capacity and project-type rules to assign the lead to an office and expert.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Attaches the uploaded proposal and its first analysis to the lead.

steps.title: Confirm, remind and prepare the expert
keyFacts: The buyer receives a confirmation and a reminder with the office address or video link and a checklist of documents to bring (pay slips, savings statements, compromis if signed).
The expert sees the simulation results, certificate, project type and uploaded documents in the workbench before the appointment starts.
painPoints: Buyers arrive without documents, so the appointment becomes an intake instead of a comparison.
Reminders in the wrong language for a buyer who booked on the French-language brand.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator
dependencies.how: Sends confirmations, reminders and the preparation checklist for the appointment.

dependencies.name: Identity, Consent and Access Control
dependencies.how: Creates the buyer's account and records the consent needed to keep their data before the appointment.

steps.title: Hold the appointment and agree the next step
keyFacts: The expert maps the buyer's situation and project in the office or on video, explains that the service is free because the chosen bank pays a referral commission, and agrees the next step: a comparison, a feasibility certificate or a file.
The outcome is recorded on the lead so the franchisee's conversion dashboard reflects held, converted and lost appointments.
painPoints: Appointments that end without a recorded outcome distort conversion reporting and are never followed up.
Video appointments with unstable connections push buyers back to their own bank branch.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator
dependencies.how: Records attendance and the agreed next step on the appointment.

dependencies.name: Lead Routing and Distribution
dependencies.how: Updates the lead to held, converted, rescheduled or lost for office reporting.

streams.name: Compare Mortgage Offers Across Banks
streams.description: From a mapped situation and project to an independent recommendation of the best total package: the workbench pulls the daily conditions of 25 banks, the expert enters the buyer's project once, the comparison engine simulates each bank's rate, fees, required insurance and conditions on the same screen, proposals received elsewhere (uploaded or brought to the office) are placed in the same comparison, and the advice is recorded with its suitability reasoning as the FSMA-regulated advice record. The buyer pays nothing extra whether they go directly to the bank or through the broker.
outcomes: Banks compared per file stays at the full 25, so buyers see the total cost of the best packages on one page instead of visiting banks one by one
Every recommendation is documented in a signed advice record before file submission, so it stands up to FSMA review and to the buyer's own bank proposal
Proposal review turnaround time stays within one working day, so households stop shopping and commit to a file

flows.title: From Situation to Recommended Package
flows.description: The expert enters the buyer's situation and project, runs the 25-bank comparison, explains the best total package including required insurance and records the advice.
flows.trigger: An appointment ended with the decision to compare, or a feasibility certificate holder has an accepted bid.
flows.successSignal: The buyer has chosen a bank from the comparison, the advice record is signed and the file can be assembled.

steps.title: Load the daily conditions of 25 banks
keyFacts: Rate sheets and conditions of the 25 partner banks are refreshed daily so every comparison uses the same day's rates, fixed and variable formulas, quotity limits and fee schedules.
Promotions and conditions tied to insurance or account bundles are stored per bank so the total-package view is complete.
painPoints: A bank sends its new rate sheet late or in a changed format and the workbench compares yesterday's rate.
Regional or campaign-specific rates that only some offices know about are not in the feed.

dependencies.name: Daily Bank Rate and Conditions Feed
dependencies.how: Ingests and validates the daily rate and conditions sheets of the 25 banks.

dependencies.name: Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds
dependencies.how: Holds the bank's product catalogue and the referral agreement behind each product.

dependencies.name: Integration Gateway
dependencies.how: Connects to bank rate feeds and file formats through one gateway.

steps.title: Enter the buyer's situation and project once
keyFacts: The expert records income, household composition, savings, existing credits, the property, purchase price, EPC label, renovation budget and preferred term in one form reused by every bank simulation.
Self-employed buyers, new builds and second homes have extra fields for the bank-specific rules that apply to them.
painPoints: Data entered during the appointment does not match the documents later collected for the file, forcing a re-comparison.
Buyers who hide an existing consumer credit get a recommendation that no bank will honour.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Stores the situation and project parameters for the comparison run.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Pre-creates the credit file so documents collected later map to the same situation.

steps.title: Run the same-screen comparison
keyFacts: The engine simulates the loan at every eligible bank and ranks offers by total cost over the term, showing rate, monthly repayment, fees, required outstanding-balance and fire insurance and the bank's usual turnaround.
The comparison is free for the buyer; the bank whose loan is concluded pays hypotheek.winkel a referral commission, which does not change the buyer's rate.
painPoints: Banks that require the buyer to move their salary account or take bundled insurance make the cheapest headline rate not the cheapest package.
An expert who favours banks with the fastest turnaround over the cheapest offer is hard to spot without the ranking being recorded.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Simulates and ranks offers across the 25 banks on total cost and conditions.

dependencies.name: Daily Bank Rate and Conditions Feed
dependencies.how: Supplies the day's rate and conditions used in each simulation.

steps.title: Explain the best total package
keyFacts: The expert walks the buyer through the top offers, the trade-offs between rate, flexibility and insurance and the effect of the renovation obligation or a longer term, and prints or e-mails the comparison as a PDF.
Buyers can compare the expert's shortlist with a proposal from their own bank on the same page.
painPoints: Rates change between the comparison and the moment the buyer decides, so the printed comparison is outdated within days.
Buyers are overwhelmed by 25 lines and want a single recommendation.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Produces the comparison PDF and shortlist shared with the buyer.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Places an uploaded or brought proposal alongside the shortlist.

steps.title: Record the advice and suitability
keyFacts: The recommendation, the alternatives considered and why the package suits the buyer's needs and repayment capacity are recorded as the advice record required of a credit intermediary registered with the FSMA.
The buyer confirms the advice and chooses the bank; the chosen bank and product are locked on the file.
painPoints: Advice records written after the fact from memory are incomplete when a complaint or inspection arrives.
A buyer who chooses a bank against the advice needs the deviation recorded explicitly.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Captures recommendation, alternatives, suitability reasoning and the buyer's confirmation.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Locks the chosen bank and product on the comparison result.

flows.title: Review a Proposal Received Elsewhere
flows.description: A buyer or refinancer uploads a proposal from their own bank through 'upload je voorstel'; the expert compares it with the 25-bank conditions and gives a quick verdict.
flows.trigger: A household received a mortgage or insurance proposal from their own bank or another broker and uploads it for a free check.
flows.successSignal: The household has a written verdict within a day: the proposal is confirmed as good, or a better package is offered with an appointment to proceed.

steps.title: Upload the proposal
keyFacts: The upload form takes the proposal PDF or photo, the household's contact details and consent, and asks for the loan amount, term and rate so the first analysis can start before an expert looks at it.
The upload is a lead routed to the nearest office like any other request.
painPoints: Proposals uploaded as blurry photos have to be requested again.
Households expect an instant answer and lose interest when the review takes several days.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Captures the proposal document, key figures and consent and creates the lead.

steps.title: Extract the proposal terms
keyFacts: The expert reads or the intake extracts rate, term, amount, fees, insurance conditions and any bundle requirements from the proposal into the same structure the comparison engine uses.
Missing data is requested by phone or e-mail before the comparison runs.
painPoints: Proposals expressed with different fee structures are hard to compare like for like.
The proposal's rate is a promotional rate that expires before the household can act.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Structures the proposal's rate, term, fees and conditions.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Maps the proposal into the comparison engine's offer structure.

steps.title: Compare against 25 banks
keyFacts: The comparison engine ranks the proposal against the day's conditions of 25 banks on total cost over the term, including the cost of required insurance.
If the proposal is competitive, the expert says so; independence is the reason the buyer pays nothing extra via the broker.
painPoints: A better offer exists only at a bank with a slow turnaround, which a refinancer with a deadline cannot use.
The household's own bank matches the better offer afterwards and the broker earns nothing for the work.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Ranks the uploaded proposal against the 25-bank offers.

dependencies.name: Daily Bank Rate and Conditions Feed
dependencies.how: Supplies the rate sheets used in the ranking.

steps.title: Give the verdict and next step
keyFacts: The household receives a short written verdict: confirmed, or a better package with the savings over the term, and an invitation to an appointment to proceed.
The verdict and the comparison are stored as the advice record for the case.
painPoints: Verdicts sent by e-mail without a call are not acted upon.
Households use the verdict to renegotiate with their own bank without telling the expert.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Stores the verdict and its reasoning as an advice record.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Sends the verdict and appointment invitation to the household.

steps.title: Convert to a file when the package is better
keyFacts: When the household proceeds, the situation captured for the review becomes the credit file and the comparison result is locked on it.
For refinancing, the case is opened as a refinancing case with the early-repayment and re-registration costs included.
painPoints: The household proceeds weeks later and the rates that made the package better are gone.

dependencies.how: Opens the credit file from the review data.

dependencies.how: Links the advice record to the new file.

streams.name: Assemble and Submit the Loan File
streams.description: From document collection to a complete credit file the chosen bank can approve quickly: the expert requests and checks pay slips, tax returns, savings statements, identity documents, the compromis and the EPC certificate, the file is assembled in the bank's expected format and submitted through the integration gateway or the bank's broker portal, approval is tracked with the bank's questions and conditions, and the outcome is recorded on the file. File first-time completeness is what drives the days from first appointment to approval, the north star of the buyer, and the file approval turnaround the bank cares about.
outcomes: File first-time-complete rate rises, so File approval turnaround time is measured in days rather than weeks
Days from first appointment to loan approval falls because missing documents are chased automatically and buyers always know what the bank is waiting for
Every submission, question and condition is traceable in the audit trail for the buyer, the office and the compliance record

flows.title: From Document Request to Bank Approval
flows.description: The expert collects and checks the buyer's documents, assembles the file, submits it to the chosen bank, follows the bank's questions and records approval and conditions.
flows.trigger: The buyer confirmed the advice and chose a bank, and a compromis is signed or imminent.
flows.successSignal: The bank has approved the loan, its conditions are recorded and the buyer has the offer to sign.

steps.title: Request the documents with a personal checklist
keyFacts: The file generates a checklist per buyer and bank: identity cards, last pay slips, tax return, proof of savings and own contribution, existing credit statements, the compromis, the EPC certificate and, for self-employed buyers, accounts and tax assessments.
Buyers upload through their account or bring documents to the office; each upload is tied to the checklist item it satisfies.
painPoints: Buyers send documents by e-mail and WhatsApp in random order and the expert spends hours sorting them.
Couples where one partner is self-employed underestimate how many documents the bank needs.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Generates the per-bank document checklist and receives the uploads against it.

dependencies.name: Identity, Consent and Access Control
dependencies.how: Authenticates the buyer and records consent for processing income and identity data.

steps.title: Check completeness and consistency
keyFacts: The expert verifies that the income on the pay slips matches the situation used in the comparison, that savings cover notary costs and own contribution, and that the compromis figures match the loan request.
The buyer's consent for the bank to consult the Central Individual Credit Register is recorded on the file.
painPoints: Income entered at the appointment turns out to be lower on the pay slips and the chosen bank no longer fits.
Documents expire (pay slips older than three months) while the buyer looks for the missing ones.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Marks the file complete only when every checklist item is present and consistent.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Flags when verified data deviates from the situation the advice was based on.

steps.title: Assemble and submit to the chosen bank
keyFacts: The file is packaged in the bank's format (broker portal upload, structured message or documented e-mail) with the expert's cover note, the advice record and the comparison result, and submitted through the integration gateway.
The submission timestamp starts the turnaround clock the bank is measured on.
painPoints: Each of the 25 banks has its own portal, forms and naming rules; a wrongly named PDF sends the file back.
Submissions made on Friday are not opened before Tuesday at some banks.

dependencies.name: Bank Submission and Approval Tracking
dependencies.how: Assembles the submission for the chosen bank and records the timestamp.

dependencies.name: Integration Gateway
dependencies.how: Delivers the file through the bank's portal or interface.

steps.title: Track the bank's questions and approval
keyFacts: The bank's questions, requests for extra documents and status changes are logged on the file, and the buyer is informed at each step.
Approval arrives with conditions (insurance, salary account, valuation) that the expert records and explains.
painPoints: Bank turnaround stretches when the credit analyst asks one question at a time.
The buyer's suspensive-condition deadline in the compromis expires before the bank answers.

dependencies.name: Bank Submission and Approval Tracking
dependencies.how: Tracks bank questions, extra requests and the approval or decline decision.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Collects the extra documents the bank asks for.

steps.title: Record the decision and conditions
keyFacts: The approval, the final rate and the bank's conditions are recorded on the file; a decline triggers a re-comparison with the next-best bank using the same documents.
The file, the advice record and every exchange with the bank are retained as the intermediary's record.
painPoints: A decline late in the process leaves too little time to submit to a second bank before the deadline.
Rates changed between advice and approval, and the buyer questions the recommendation.

dependencies.name: Bank Submission and Approval Tracking
dependencies.how: Records approval, final conditions or decline.

streams.name: Close the Loan Through Notary and Insurance
streams.description: From bank approval to the keys: the expert coordinates the loan offer signature, attaches outstanding-balance (schuldsaldo) and fire insurance from the compared insurers or the bank's own, aligns the notary on the deed date, follows the disbursement and hands the household over to contract monitoring. The closing milestones (offer signed, insurance in place, deed planned, deed signed, funds released) are tracked per file, the insurance attach rate is a supporting KPI of the expert, and the concluded loan is what triggers the bank's referral commission.
outcomes: Insurance attach rate rises because outstanding-balance and fire insurance are compared across the 11 insurers and bound before every deed
Days from approval to deed fall and compromis deadlines are met because offer, insurance, notary and disbursement milestones are tracked per file
Every concluded loan and its attached policies are registered in the contract vault and in commission reconciliation on the deed date

flows.title: From Approval to Deed and Disbursement
flows.description: The expert guides the buyer through the offer signature, insurance, notary coordination, deed and disbursement, and hands the contracts to the household vault.
flows.trigger: The bank has approved the loan and issued the offer.
flows.successSignal: The deed is signed, the funds are released, the insurance is active and the household's contracts are in the vault.

steps.title: Sign the loan offer
keyFacts: The buyer signs the bank's loan offer, on paper in the office or electronically, within the offer's validity period; the expert checks the final rate against the approval.
The offer signature date is a milestone on the file.
painPoints: Rates changed between proposal and offer, and the buyer wants to reopen the comparison.
Offers with short validity expire during the buyer's holiday.

dependencies.name: Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking
dependencies.how: Tracks the offer validity and signature milestone.

dependencies.name: Bank Submission and Approval Tracking
dependencies.how: Provides the approved rate and conditions for the check.

steps.title: Attach outstanding-balance and fire insurance
keyFacts: The expert compares outstanding-balance and fire insurance across the 11 insurers and the bank's own offer, explains the bank's conditions for a rate reduction and binds the chosen policies before the deed.
Outstanding-balance insurance may require health questions or a medical examination; the timeline is planned so acceptance arrives before the deed date.
painPoints: Medical acceptance for outstanding-balance insurance takes weeks for older buyers or those with a health history.
The bank grants a rate reduction only for its own insurance, and the comparison must show the total cost either way.

dependencies.name: Insurance Quote and Policy Binding
dependencies.how: Quotes and binds the outstanding-balance and fire policies.

dependencies.name: Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking
dependencies.how: Records the insurance-in-place milestone required for disbursement.

steps.title: Coordinate the notary and deed date
keyFacts: The expert aligns the notary, the bank and the buyer on the deed date within the four months after the compromis, sends the bank's deed instructions and checks that the mortgage mandate or registration is prepared.
Deed dates and notary contacts are tracked as milestones so nothing is missed in the last weeks.
painPoints: Notaries are booked out and the deed slips past the compromis deadline.
The bank's instructions reach the notary late and the deed is postponed on the day.

dependencies.name: Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking
dependencies.how: Tracks the deed date, notary contact and bank instructions.

dependencies.name: Integration Gateway
dependencies.how: Exchanges documents and instructions with the bank and e-signature service.

steps.title: Sign the deed and release the funds
keyFacts: The deed is signed at the notary, the bank releases the funds to the notary and the purchase is completed; the expert confirms disbursement on the file.
The concluded loan is the event that entitles hypotheek.winkel to the bank's referral commission.
painPoints: Disbursement is delayed because a condition (valuation, salary account) was not closed.
Buyers who never hear from the expert after the deed do not come back for their next project.

dependencies.name: Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking
dependencies.how: Records the deed signature and disbursement milestones.

dependencies.name: Commission Reconciliation and Network Payout
dependencies.how: Registers the concluded loan for commission reconciliation with the bank.

steps.title: Hand over to the household vault
keyFacts: The loan, the outstanding-balance and fire policies and their renewal dates are stored in the household's contract vault so Peasy can keep an eye on them and warn when a better option exists.
The expert invites the household to compare energy and telecom for the new home, the start of the household relationship.
painPoints: Contracts closed on paper are not entered into the vault and monitoring never starts.
Buyers moving into the new home are overloaded and ignore the energy and telecom invitation.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Stores the loan and policies with renewal dates in the household vault.

dependencies.name: Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking
dependencies.how: Closes the file with the handover recorded.

streams.name: Refinance or Extend an Existing Loan
streams.description: Serve the owner who already has a loan: a rate drop that makes refinancing worthwhile, the Flemish renovation obligation for a low-EPC home, a second home, a new build or financing as a self-employed person. The case starts from the existing loan and the new need, computes whether refinancing beats the early-repayment and re-registration costs or whether an additional loan is better, compares the 25 banks for the new structure and reuses the file process, with loan-linked insurance re-checked at the end. Savings identified per refinancing case is the north star of this customer.
outcomes: Savings identified per refinancing case is computed net of reinvestment fee, notary and registration costs, so owners get an honest answer quickly
Refinancing conversion rate rises because renovation, second-home and new-build projects are financed on top of the existing situation without starting from scratch
Loan-linked outstanding-balance and fire insurance is re-compared with every change, lifting Insurance attach rate on refinancing files

flows.title: From Rate Change to Refinancing Case
flows.description: An owner asks whether their current loan can be beaten; the expert computes the refinancing break-even, compares banks and opens a case when it pays.
flows.trigger: Rates have dropped, the owner's bank sent a proposal, or a monitoring alert suggested that the loan can be refinanced.
flows.successSignal: The owner has a documented decision: refinance with a chosen bank and a case in progress, or keep the loan because it does not pay off.

steps.title: Capture the existing loan and the trigger
keyFacts: The owner enters or uploads the current loan: outstanding balance, rate, remaining term, bank and any proposal received; a saved simulation or the contract vault pre-fills what Peasy already knows.
The trigger (rate drop, own-bank proposal, need for cash for a renovation) determines which case type is opened.
painPoints: Owners do not know their exact outstanding balance and remaining term without digging up the repayment table.
Proposals from the own bank are often a rate reduction offered to keep the client, with conditions hidden in the small print.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Opens the refinancing or extension case with the existing loan data and trigger.

dependencies.name: Upload-Your-Proposal Intake
dependencies.how: Captures the proposal received elsewhere for review.

steps.title: Compute the break-even after costs
keyFacts: The case computes early-repayment indemnity, release and re-registration costs, notary costs and the new monthly repayment, and shows whether the savings over the remaining term beat those costs.
Internal refinancing at the own bank and external refinancing at another bank are shown side by side.
painPoints: Costs differ per bank and per notary, so the break-even is a range rather than a number.
Owners with few years left expect savings that the costs eat up.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Computes costs, savings and break-even for the refinancing scenarios.

dependencies.name: Daily Bank Rate and Conditions Feed
dependencies.how: Supplies the day's rates for the new-loan scenarios.

steps.title: Compare the new structure across banks
keyFacts: The comparison engine ranks the 25 banks for the new loan amount and term, including the cost of moving the outstanding-balance insurance if the bank requires it.
The advice record documents why refinancing does or does not pay and which bank fits.
painPoints: Rates move between the break-even calculation and the decision, changing the answer.
The best bank requires a new medical acceptance for the insurance that the owner may no longer pass.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Ranks the 25 banks for the refinancing structure.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Records the refinancing recommendation and its reasoning.

steps.title: Open the file and collect documents
keyFacts: When refinancing pays, the case becomes a credit file with the owner's documents plus the current loan statement and the repayment table from the existing bank.
The file follows the standard submission and approval tracking.
painPoints: The existing bank is slow to provide the release figures needed for the new bank.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Creates the credit file with the refinancing-specific documents.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Tracks the case through file, approval and closing.

steps.title: Close the case and record the savings
keyFacts: After the deed, the savings identified and realised are recorded on the case, and the new loan replaces the old one in the household vault.
Owners who decided not to refinance get a note in the vault so monitoring can re-check when rates move again.
painPoints: Savings recorded at advice time differ from realised savings when the final rate changed.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Records identified and realised savings on the closed case.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Keeps the advice record of the decision, including 'do not refinance'.

flows.title: Finance a Renovation, Second Home or New Build
flows.description: An owner needs financing on top of the existing loan for a renovation (including the EPC renovation obligation), a second home or a new build; the case is checked for feasibility and structured across banks.
flows.trigger: An owner plans a renovation, buys a second home or starts a new build, or the bank requires the renovation obligation of a low-EPC home to be financed.
flows.successSignal: The additional loan or renovation loan is approved with a structure that respects the existing loan and the owner's repayment capacity.

steps.title: Describe the project and the EPC situation
keyFacts: The owner describes the project: renovation budget and quotes, the EPC label and the renovation obligation for low-EPC homes bought in Flanders, or the second home or new-build plan with its instalment schedule.
Simulators for the additional monthly repayment give a first idea before the appointment.
painPoints: Renovation budgets grow after the first quotes, and the loan is too small.
Owners are unaware that a low-EPC home must be renovated within the legal period after purchase.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Opens the renovation, second-home or new-build case with project data.

dependencies.name: Feasibility Check and Certificate
dependencies.how: Checks whether the project is feasible on top of the existing loan.

steps.title: Check feasibility on top of the existing loan
keyFacts: The expert checks the combined repayment burden of existing and new loans against the banks' limits and the owner's income, and whether the existing bank or a new one should carry the additional loan.
For new builds the bank releases funds in tranches against invoices, which the case models.
painPoints: The existing loan is at a bank that does not offer renovation loans at a competitive rate, but moving both loans costs too much.
Self-employed owners need accounts and tax assessments that are not yet available for the last year.

dependencies.name: Feasibility Check and Certificate
dependencies.how: Computes the combined repayment burden and feasibility.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Compares banks for the additional loan or a full restructuring.

steps.title: Structure and compare the additional loan
keyFacts: The case compares an additional loan at the existing bank, a renovation loan elsewhere, or refinancing everything at a new bank, and records the recommendation with suitability reasoning.
painPoints: Comparing three structures across 25 banks produces more options than the owner can absorb.

dependencies.name: Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine
dependencies.how: Ranks the structures and banks on total cost.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Records the recommended structure and alternatives.

steps.title: Assemble the file with quotes and plans
keyFacts: The file collects contractor quotes, building permits, plans, the EPC certificate and, for second homes, the compromis, next to the standard income documents.
The file is submitted to the chosen bank and tracked to approval.
painPoints: Banks pay renovation loans against invoices, and owners who paid contractors upfront cannot draw the loan.

dependencies.name: Credit File and Document Collection
dependencies.how: Collects quotes, permits, plans and EPC certificate on the file.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Tracks the case through submission and approval.

steps.title: Re-check the loan-linked insurance
keyFacts: Once the additional loan is approved, outstanding-balance and fire insurance are re-checked so the cover matches the new total and the renovated or second property.
painPoints: Owners forget to extend fire insurance to the second home until a claim.

dependencies.name: Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases
dependencies.how: Flags the loan-linked insurance to be re-compared after the change.

dependencies.name: Advice Record and Suitability Assessment
dependencies.how: Records the insurance recommendation for the new situation.

rootGroups.name: Comparison and Switching Journeys
rootGroups.description: Insurance across 11 insurers, electricity and gas for every meter and solar situation, internet, TV and mobile under Easy Switch, executed by customer care in Hasselt and Oujda or in self-service, with the household contract vault, budget barometer and savings alerts that keep Peasy watching every contract it brokered.

streams.name: Compare and Switch Insurance
streams.description: From a car, fire, funeral or outstanding-balance comparison on Verzekeringen.be, Aanbieders.be or peasy.be across 11 insurers to a bound policy and the cancellation of the old one: the household enters the risk, the comparison module prices it at every insurer from the tariff feeds, an advisor in Hasselt or Oujda checks the cover, answers the questions and binds the policy through the insurer's system, and the old contract is cancelled within its notice window so the household is never double-insured or uninsured. The household pays nothing extra; the insurer pays a referral fee per concluded contract.
outcomes: Households compare the 11 insurers on price and cover in minutes and bind the chosen policy in the same contact, lifting First-contact resolution rate
Switch error rate falls because old policies are cancelled within the notice window, without a gap or a double premium
Switches won through comparison rise for partners because quotes match the insurer's tariff and bind without re-quoting

flows.title: From Comparison to Bound Policy and Cancelled Old Contract
flows.description: A household compares car or fire insurance, an advisor confirms the cover and binds the policy, and the old contract is cancelled within its notice window.
flows.trigger: A household sees on the budget barometer or a renewal notice that its car or fire premium is high, or receives a monitoring alert.
flows.successSignal: The new policy is active from the requested date, the old one is cancelled without overlap, and both documents are in the household vault.

steps.title: Enter the risk and compare 11 insurers
keyFacts: The household enters the vehicle or the home (build year, surface, contents value), the drivers or occupants, the desired cover (third-party, omnium, contents, legal assistance) and current premium; the module prices the risk across 11 insurers from the tariff feeds.
Results show premium, franchise, cover differences and the insurer's rating on one page under the Verzekeringen.be, Aanbieders.be or peasy.be brand.
painPoints: Households compare a cheaper third-party quote with their current omnium and think they save more than they do.
A tariff feed error at one insurer shows a premium the insurer will not honour at binding.

dependencies.name: Insurance Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Prices the risk across the 11 insurers and presents cover differences.

dependencies.name: Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds
dependencies.how: Supplies the insurers' product definitions and tariff feeds.

steps.title: Talk to an advisor about the cover
keyFacts: An advisor in Hasselt or Oujda calls back or takes the chat, checks that the cover matches the household's needs (young driver, home office, solar panels on the roof) and explains franchise and exclusions using the knowledge base scripts.
The conversation is logged as a ticket so a colleague can continue if the household calls again.
painPoints: Households who answered the risk questions loosely get a different premium once the advisor asks the insurer's exact questions.
Advisors cannot answer edge cases about exclusions and put the household on hold while they search.

dependencies.name: Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox
dependencies.how: Logs the call or chat and the advice given on the ticket.

dependencies.name: Advisor Knowledge Base and Scripts
dependencies.how: Provides the cover-check script and insurer-specific answers.

steps.title: Request the quote and answer the insurer's questions
keyFacts: The advisor requests the binding quote from the chosen insurer through the gateway with the complete risk data, claims history and, for outstanding-balance cover, the health questions; the insurer confirms the premium and acceptance.
Documents (identity card, registration certificate, previous policy) are collected on the ticket.
painPoints: Claims history not disclosed at comparison leads to a higher premium or refusal at quote stage.
Insurers that only accept quotes by e-mail add days to what the household expected to be an instant switch.

dependencies.name: Insurance Quote and Policy Binding
dependencies.how: Requests and stores the insurer's binding quote and acceptance.

dependencies.name: Integration Gateway
dependencies.how: Sends the quote request to the insurer's system.

steps.title: Bind the policy with the start date
keyFacts: The household signs the application electronically, the policy is bound with a start date aligned to the end of the old contract's notice period, and the insurer issues the policy document and, for cars, the green card.
The contract is concluded with the insurer, never with Peasy, which is how Peasy stays independent.
painPoints: A start date set before the old policy ends means a double premium; one set after leaves a gap.

dependencies.name: Insurance Quote and Policy Binding
dependencies.how: Binds the policy and stores the policy document.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Stores the new policy and its renewal date in the household vault.

steps.title: Cancel the old contract within the notice window
keyFacts: The advisor prepares the cancellation letter for the old insurer with the household's mandate, respecting the annual expiry date and the notice period, and sends it by registered mail or through the insurer channel.
Cancellation confirmations are tracked and the household is told when the old premium stops.
painPoints: Old contracts renew tacitly for a year when the notice window is missed by a day.
Some insurers require the household's own signed letter and reject the broker's cancellation.

dependencies.name: Cancellation and Old-Contract Termination
dependencies.how: Generates, sends and tracks the cancellation of the old policy.

dependencies.name: Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox
dependencies.how: Keeps the ticket open until the old insurer confirms.

steps.title: Confirm and close the request
keyFacts: The household receives both confirmations and the policies in the vault; the ticket is closed as resolved in one contact where possible, which is what the advisor is measured on.
painPoints: Households call back weeks later because the old insurer still sent a premium notice.

dependencies.name: Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox
dependencies.how: Closes the ticket with the first-contact-resolution outcome.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Makes both policy documents available in the household account.

streams.name: Compare and Switch Energy Contracts
streams.description: From postcode, meter type, digital meter and solar-panel data to an electricity and gas comparison and a switch executed with the new supplier on Aanbieders.be, Mesfournisseurs.be or peasy.be: the household enters consumption or an annual invoice, the module prices every supplier's tariff card for its situation (single or dual-rate meter, digital meter, solar panels and the prosumer tariff, gas), an advisor confirms the choice and places the switch order with the new supplier, who takes over from the old one without interruption. Aanbieders.be claims savings of up to hundreds of euros a year; the VREG V-test remains the public reference in Flanders.
outcomes: Households see the cheapest electricity and gas contracts for their exact meter situation within minutes, and Contracts switched per household rises
Switch error rate falls because the new supplier executes the switch without interruption and the household never writes to the old one
Tariff feed accuracy is verified before release, so the price quoted is the price invoiced

flows.title: From Meter Data to Executed Switch
flows.description: A household compares energy contracts for its meter and solar situation, confirms with an advisor and has the switch executed by the new supplier.
flows.trigger: A household receives a high annual settlement, sees on the budget barometer that its energy cost is above the Belgian average, or its fixed contract ends.
flows.successSignal: The new supplier has confirmed the switch date, the old contract ends automatically and the contract is in the household vault.

steps.title: Enter postcode, meter type and consumption
keyFacts: The household enters postcode, whether it has a single-rate, dual-rate or digital meter, annual consumption in kWh and m3 (or uploads the annual invoice), gas connection, solar panels and whether the prosumer tariff or injection applies.
The budget barometer pre-fills consumption for households that already benchmarked their fixed costs.
painPoints: Households do not know their annual consumption and guess, which makes the ranking wrong.
Solar-panel owners with a digital meter do not understand injection tariffs and the end of the reversing meter.

dependencies.name: Energy Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Captures meter type, consumption, gas, solar and prosumer data.

dependencies.name: Budget Barometer
dependencies.how: Supplies the household's benchmarked energy cost and consumption.

steps.title: Compare suppliers on the tariff cards
keyFacts: The module prices every supplier's fixed and variable tariff cards for the household's profile, including network costs and levies, and shows the estimated annual cost and the saving versus the current contract.
Tariff cards are refreshed from the suppliers' feeds; the VREG V-test and V-check with the invoice code are the public reference the ranking must be consistent with.
painPoints: A supplier's tariff card changes mid-month and the feed lags, so a household is quoted a price that no longer exists.
Variable contracts indexed on different parameters are hard to compare on one annual estimate.

dependencies.name: Energy Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Prices and ranks all suppliers' tariff cards for the profile.

dependencies.name: Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds
dependencies.how: Supplies validated supplier tariff cards and product terms.

steps.title: Confirm the choice with an advisor
keyFacts: An advisor confirms the chosen contract by phone or chat, checks the EAN numbers of the electricity and gas connections, the meter reading approach and the desired switch date, and explains fixed versus variable pricing.
Households can also complete the switch in self-service; the advisor steps in for callbacks and questions.
painPoints: EAN numbers are on the old invoice that the household cannot find.
Households want to switch before their fixed contract ends and face a cancellation fee they were not aware of.

dependencies.name: Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox
dependencies.how: Logs the confirmation call and the data collected.

dependencies.name: Energy Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Locks the chosen supplier and tariff on the comparison.

steps.title: Place the switch order with the new supplier
keyFacts: The switch order with identity, address, EAN numbers, meter type, requested start date and mandate is sent to the new supplier through the gateway; the new supplier notifies the old one and the grid operator, so the household does not cancel anything itself.
The order status is tracked until the supplier confirms the start date.
painPoints: Suppliers reject orders when the name on the order does not match the name on the connection.
Switch confirmations take weeks with some suppliers, and households call to ask what happened.

dependencies.name: Energy and Telecom Switch Execution
dependencies.how: Creates, sends and tracks the switch order.

dependencies.name: Integration Gateway
dependencies.how: Delivers the order through the supplier's interface.

steps.title: Confirm the start and store the contract
keyFacts: The supplier's confirmation, contract and start date are stored in the household vault with the contract end date, so monitoring can re-compare before the next renewal.
The concluded switch is what the supplier pays a referral fee for.
painPoints: Households receive a final settlement from the old supplier that surprises them and blame the switch.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Stores the energy contract, EAN data and end date in the vault.

dependencies.name: Energy and Telecom Switch Execution
dependencies.how: Marks the switch as completed on the supplier's confirmation.

streams.name: Compare and Switch Telecom and Mobile
streams.description: From current internet, TV, fixed-line and mobile usage to the cheapest pack and a switch under BIPT Easy Switch: the household enters its current operator, pack and usage (download needs, TV channels, number of mobile lines and data), the module compares operators' packs and mobile plans at the household's address, and the advisor places the order with the new operator, who terminates the old fixed contract through Easy Switch while the mobile numbers are ported. Aanbieders.be positions telecom as a further saving after energy, and telecom switches are often bundled with the energy call.
outcomes: Households find the cheapest pack for their real usage and address in one comparison, and Switches completed per advisor per day rises
Fixed switches run under BIPT Easy Switch and mobile numbers are ported without the household chasing the old operator, keeping Switch error rate low
Telecom is switched in the same contact as energy where the household wants it, raising Contracts switched per household

flows.title: From Usage to Easy Switch
flows.description: A household compares internet, TV and mobile packs for its address and usage, and the advisor orders the new pack with the old contract terminated through Easy Switch.
flows.trigger: A promotional period ends and the household's telecom invoice jumps, or the energy call ends with the question whether telecom can be cheaper too.
flows.successSignal: The new pack is installed or activated, the mobile numbers are ported, the old contract is terminated through Easy Switch and the contract is in the vault.

steps.title: Describe the current pack and usage
keyFacts: The household enters the address, the current operator and pack, the monthly price, the number of mobile lines and data use, TV needs and whether a fixed line is still used.
The comparison distinguishes packs available at the address (cable, fibre, copper) from those that are not.
painPoints: Households overestimate the TV channels they need and underestimate mobile data.
Address availability data is wrong for new streets and split houses.

dependencies.name: Telecom and Mobile Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Captures address, current pack, lines and usage.

steps.title: Compare packs and mobile plans
keyFacts: The module ranks operators' packs and mobile plans for the usage, showing monthly price after promotions, installation costs and the saving versus the current pack.
Operator tariffs and promotions come from the partner catalogue and change frequently.
painPoints: Promotions that last six months make the first-year price and the ongoing price differ, and households compare the wrong one.
An operator changes its pack line-up and the catalogue still lists the old packs.

dependencies.name: Telecom and Mobile Comparison Module
dependencies.how: Ranks packs and mobile plans on monthly cost after promotions.

dependencies.name: Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds
dependencies.how: Supplies pack definitions, prices and promotion periods.

steps.title: Check the old contract and Easy Switch conditions
keyFacts: The advisor checks the old contract's minimum term and any remaining device instalments, collects the Easy Switch ID from the old operator's invoice and the mobile numbers to port, and agrees the switch date.
Under BIPT Easy Switch the new fixed operator terminates the old contract on the household's behalf.
painPoints: Households cannot find the Easy Switch ID on their invoice.
Old contracts with unpaid device instalments trigger a final invoice the household did not expect.

dependencies.name: Cancellation and Old-Contract Termination
dependencies.how: Records the old contract's term, Easy Switch ID and termination path.

dependencies.name: Telecom and Mobile Comparison Module

streams.name: Monitor Household Contracts and Alert Savings
streams.description: The household relationship after the transaction: every brokered loan, policy, energy and telecom contract is stored per household with its renewal, expiry and promotion dates, the budget barometer benchmarks the household's fixed costs against Belgian averages, monitoring re-compares each contract against current tariffs and rates, and a savings alert invites the household to switch again by self-service or with an advisor. This is the cross-sell engine that turns one mortgage into a household that also insures, switches energy and telecom through Peasy, and the source of the annual household savings north star.
outcomes: No brokered contract passes its renewal or promotion end while a cheaper option exists, raising Annual household savings realised
Savings alert acceptance rate rises because alerts are accurate, above threshold and sent in the household's language
Contracts switched per household grows as a mortgage household becomes a multi-contract household through timely cross-sell

flows.title: From Stored Contract to Savings Alert and New Switch
flows.description: Contracts stored in the vault are re-compared against current tariffs, a savings alert goes to the household and a new switch is started when the household accepts.
flows.trigger: A brokered contract approaches its renewal or promotion end, or a tariff or rate move makes a cheaper option available.
flows.successSignal: The household accepted the alert and a new comparison and switch are in progress, or declined with a reason recorded for the next cycle.

steps.title: Store every brokered contract with its dates
keyFacts: Each concluded loan, policy, energy and telecom contract is stored in the household vault with provider, product, price, start date, renewal or expiry date, promotion end and notice period.
The household sees all contracts in its account and can add contracts concluded elsewhere.
painPoints: Contracts closed in the office on paper or by e-mail are not entered and never monitored.
Households do not add contracts concluded elsewhere, so the vault stays incomplete.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Stores contracts with their dates and documents per household.

steps.title: Benchmark the fixed costs with the budget barometer
keyFacts: The budget barometer compares the household's mortgage, insurance, energy and telecom costs with the Belgian averages for a similar household and shows where it overpays.
The barometer is also the entry point for households that have not brokered anything yet.
painPoints: Averages hide that a household with an electric car or a large house legitimately pays more.

dependencies.name: Budget Barometer
dependencies.how: Computes the household's fixed-cost position versus Belgian averages.

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account
dependencies.how: Feeds the stored contract prices into the barometer.

steps.title: Re-compare each contract before renewal
keyFacts: Monitoring runs each stored contract through the insurance, energy and telecom comparison modules ahead of its renewal or promotion end, using current tariff feeds, and computes the potential saving.
Rate movements trigger a refinancing check for stored loans.
painPoints: Re-comparison based on old consumption or risk data produces savings that vanish when checked.
Tariff feed errors create false alerts that erode trust.

dependencies.name: Renewal Monitoring and Savings Alerts
dependencies.how: Schedules and runs re-comparisons per contract and date.

dependencies.name: Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds

dependencies.name: Telecom and Mobile Comparison Module

steps.title: Send a savings alert the household can act on
keyFacts: The household receives an alert with the saving, the proposed contract and a one-click way to switch or to be called back; alerts below a threshold are suppressed.
Savings alert acceptance rate is tracked per contract type.
painPoints: Too many small alerts and the household unsubscribes.
Alerts sent in the wrong language or for a contract the household already cancelled.

dependencies.name: Renewal Monitoring and Savings Alerts
dependencies.how: Creates and sends the savings alert with the proposed action.

dependencies.name: Customer 360 and Cross-sell Engine
dependencies.how: Uses the household profile to decide timing, channel and threshold.

steps.title: Accept the alert and start the switch
keyFacts: Acceptance opens the comparison pre-filled from the vault and hands over to the insurance, energy or telecom switch flow; a decline records the reason for the next cycle.
painPoints: Households accept but never complete the self-service switch, and no advisor follows up.

dependencies.name: Renewal Monitoring and Savings Alerts

dependencies.name: Household Contract Vault and Customer Account

steps.title: Propose the next relevant contract

dependencies.name: Customer 360 and Cross-sell Engine

dependencies.name: Renewal Monitoring and Savings Alerts
dependencies.how: Sends the cross-sell proposal as an alert.

streams.name: Serve Customers Through Customer Care
streams.description: From phone, chat, callback and e-mail contacts in Hasselt and Oujda to resolved requests: every contact becomes a ticket in the omnichannel inbox, the advisor identifies the household and sees its contracts and open cases, uses scripts and the knowledge base to answer, executes or hands over the comparison, switch or cancellation, and closes the ticket with first-contact resolution as the goal. Customer care also answers questions about brokered mortgages, routes complaints and keeps the published opening hours (Monday to Thursday until 17:00, Friday until 16:00 on Aanbieders.be).
outcomes: First-contact resolution rate rises across phone, chat, callback and e-mail for all three brands
Every advisor sees the whole household and its open cases before answering, so repeat contacts per request fall
Complaints and escalations are captured and routed into the compliance register within the deadlines rather than lost in an inbox

Callback requests are called back within the opening hours the sites publish.

French-language contacts routed to a Dutch-only queue.

rootGroups.name: Network, Partner and Compliance Journeys
rootGroups.description: The operations behind the front door: lead routing and dashboards for the franchised office network, the academy that certifies about 30 advisors a year for a scarce-skill role, the tariff feeds and commission reconciliation for more than 50 partners, and the FSMA, complaints and GDPR evidence across three brands.

streams.name: Run the Franchise Office Network
streams.description: Run the network of about 70 hypotheek.winkel offices, largely franchised, across Flanders and Brussels: onboard a new office and its franchisee, define its territory, route the leads and appointments the brand generates to it, staff it with certified experts, and give franchisees and head office production, conversion and commission dashboards per office and expert. After the Meilleurtaux acquisition the same engine has to feed a combined network of 81 offices nationwide. Qualified appointments per office per month is the franchisee's north star.
outcomes: Qualified appointments per office per month rises because every territory's leads are routed and accepted within the response window
New offices and franchisees are onboarded with territory, registered experts, tooling and compliance in place before the first appointment
Head office steers all offices on comparable production, Appointment-to-loan conversion rate and commission data per office and expert

flows.title: From Office Onboarding to Steered Production
flows.description: A franchisee opens or takes over an office, receives its territory and lead flow, and is steered on production and conversion dashboards.
flows.trigger: A franchise agreement is signed for a new or existing office, or head office reviews the monthly production of the network.
flows.successSignal: The office receives its leads, experts are registered and active, and the monthly dashboard shows appointments, files, loans and commissions per office and expert.

steps.title: Onboard the office and franchisee
keyFacts: The office is created with address, opening hours, franchise agreement, brand assets and the experts working there; each expert must be registered with the FSMA as a credit intermediary or as an employee under the office's registration before advising.
Franchisees are independent entrepreneurs who depend on the brand for appointments and pay for the brand and tooling through the commission split.
painPoints: Offices open before their experts are certified and registered, so the first weeks produce no files.
Franchisees taking over an existing office inherit territory disputes with neighbours.

dependencies.name: Multi-brand Site Shell and Language Routing

steps.title: Define the territory and lead rules
keyFacts: Each office covers a set of postcodes; lead routing rules assign simulations, bookings, callbacks and uploads by postcode, capacity and project type, with fallbacks when an office is full or closed.
Rules are adjusted when offices open, close or merge, including the integration of Meilleurtaux offices in Wallonia, Ghent and Antwerp.
painPoints: Postcodes on the border of two territories generate disputes over who owns the lead.
Rules that favour capacity starve small offices that convert better.

dependencies.name: Lead Routing and Distribution
dependencies.how: Maintains territory, capacity and fallback rules per office.

dependencies.name: Office and Franchise Management
dependencies.how: Holds the postcode territory per office.

steps.title: Feed the office with appointments
keyFacts: The brand's simulators, content and reviews generate appointments and callbacks that are routed to the office; the franchisee sees new, accepted and overdue leads and reassigns them within the office.
Local marketing support (Google reviews, local campaigns) is available from head office.
painPoints: Leads that are not accepted within a day are lost to the buyer's own bank.
Franchisees complain that leads are of low quality when the simulator inputs were unrealistic.

dependencies.name: Appointment Booking and Office Locator

dependencies.name: Lead Routing and Distribution
dependencies.how: Shows the office's lead queue with acceptance and overdue status.

steps.title: Monitor production and conversion per office
keyFacts: Dashboards show appointments held, files opened, files submitted, loans concluded, insurance attached and conversion between each step per office and per expert, monthly and year to date.
Head office compares offices and spots those needing training, staffing or lead adjustments.
painPoints: Experts who do not record appointment outcomes make their conversion look worse or better than it is.
Franchisees dispute production figures when the deed date and the commission date fall in different months.

dependencies.name: Production and Conversion Dashboards
dependencies.how: Computes and shows production and conversion per office and expert.

dependencies.name: Analytics and Data Platform
dependencies.how: Aggregates lead, appointment, file and loan events.

keyFacts: The franchisee sees the commission statement per concluded loan and policy, the network payout and disputes, and plans expert capacity with the academy pipeline.
Head office uses the same data to decide where to open offices and where to add experts.
painPoints: Commission disputes when a bank pays late or a loan is repaid early within the clawback period.
Scarce experts leave for a bank and the office cannot replace them for months.

dependencies.name: Commission Reconciliation and Network Payout

streams.name: Train and Certify Advisors in the Academy
streams.description: Grow scarce advisors in-house: the in-house academy recruits career changers and junior profiles, trains about 30 advisors per year to become mortgage experts or insurance advisors, prepares them for the professional-knowledge examinations required for FSMA registration of credit and insurance intermediaries, coaches them in an office or customer-care team and certifies them before they advise households alone. Mortgage expert is a scarce-skill role the market cannot supply, so the academy turns advisor supply into planned capacity rather than a bottleneck.
outcomes: Advisors certified per year reaches about 30, entering the office network and customer care with the required knowledge
No advisor advises households before FSMA knowledge requirements and internal certification are met
Expert retention rate improves because offices and customer care plan capacity on the academy pipeline instead of the scarce external market

flows.successSignal: The advisor holds the required knowledge certificates, is registered with the FSMA, has passed internal certification and is active in an office or care team.

steps.title: Recruit and enrol the cohort
keyFacts: The academy recruits career changers and juniors for the cohort, assesses motivation and language (Dutch, French), and enrols them with a target role (mortgage expert or insurance advisor), a target office or care team and a start date.
Franchisees can enrol their own recruits in the programme.
painPoints: Cohorts start with fewer candidates than needed because mortgage advisor is a scarce-skill role.
Franchisees want experts immediately and resent months of training.

Progress and assessments are tracked per learner.
painPoints: Course material lags behind product and regulatory changes.
Learners from Oujda need Belgian market context that the curriculum assumes.

streams.name: Manage Partners, Tariffs and Commissions
streams.description: Run the partner side of the model: contracts with more than 50 partners (25 banks, 11 insurers, energy suppliers and telecom operators) that define products, tariff feeds and referral fees, the ingestion and validation of daily bank rate sheets and partner tariff cards, the partner portal where partners see leads, concluded contracts and statements, and the reconciliation that matches every concluded loan, policy and switch to the partner's commission statement before the network payout to offices and advisors. Commission disputes and tariff feed accuracy are what this stream exists to prevent.
outcomes: Tariff feed accuracy stays high, so every partner product and tariff in the comparison modules matches what the partner invoices
Commission reconciliation cycle time falls and commissions from more than 50 partners are paid to offices and advisors on time without disputes
Partners see their leads, contracts and statements in one portal, and Switches won through comparison keeps them listed

flows.description: A partner is contracted, its products and tariffs are fed into the modules, concluded contracts are reconciled against its commission statement and the network is paid.

flows.successSignal: The partner's tariffs are live and validated, the month's commissions are reconciled with disputes resolved and the payout to offices and advisors is executed.

steps.title: Contract the partner and its referral fees
keyFacts: The partner agreement records the products in scope, the referral fee per concluded contract (per loan amount, per policy, per switch), clawback rules for early repayment or cancellation, reporting cadence and data-sharing terms.

painPoints: Fee structures differ per partner and product, making reconciliation rules complex.
Clawback rules on early repayment surprise offices months after payout.

painPoints: A partner changes its file format without notice and the feed fails silently.
Outlier rates that are real promotions are rejected as errors, or errors are published as promotions.
